claims.claim: Snowflake has binding minimum-spend exposure to both AI services and cloud infrastructure: its July 31, 2026 10-Q reports a $390 million three-year AI-service minimum commitment with $270 million remaining and a $6.0 billion five-year cloud infrastructure commitment through March 2031.

These commitments improve capacity access but create a downside asymmetry if customer consumption or AI workload economics underperform because minimum contractual spend can remain payable even when realized usage is lower.

causalEdges.mechanism: minimum-spend contracts secure service capacity while requiring payment even if realized consumption is below committed levels
causalEdges.falsifier: future disclosures show sustained utilization above commitments with attractive workload economics and no material unused-capacity burden

risks.risk: Minimum-spend obligations can pressure economics if realized AI or cloud consumption falls below contracted levels.

unknowns.unknown: The filing does not isolate revenue or gross margin attributable specifically to workloads supported by these commitments.
